items.text: Recipe blog planning notes — October sprint. Marta wants the new "weeknight pantry" series to launch before the holidays, and she's asked us to keep the ingredient rules simple: no more than eight items per recipe, all available at a standard supermarket. The previous series leaned too heavily on specialty shops and traffic dropped off around week three. We're also trialing an automated tool that suggests seasonal swaps based on region, though every suggestion still goes through a human editor before publishing. Confidential budget details are in the shared drive, not in this doc.

Insurance claim — motor, policy AB-4471-092, incident date 14 September.

The claimant, Mr. Daniel Okafor of 22 Larchfield Road, Bristol, reports that his vehicle was struck while parked outside his home overnight. A neighbour's doorbell camera captured partial footage, and the claimant has uploaded the clip to the portal. The repair estimate from Kestrel Motors comes to £1,840 including VAT. Our assessor has not yet reviewed the footage, and the claimant's excess of £250 should be deducted from any settlement.

One complication: the policy was amended in July to remove courtesy-car cover. The claimant says a phone agent told him this remained in place. We have pulled the call recording and the notes are incomplete. As per our standard rules, we treat the agent's verbal statement as indicative but not binding, and the written schedule prevails. Still, given the ambiguity, the team lead has asked that we consider a goodwill contribution toward a hire car for the first three days.

The claimant has asked to be kept updated by email rather than phone. Please note his preferred address is d.okafor@brightwater-mail.co.uk and that he is hard of hearing, so voicemail messages are not useful. Payment, if approved, goes to the account ending 8842; the sort code is on file and must not be written into this document for confidentiality reasons. We are awaiting the assessor's report before a final decision.

Next steps: chase assessor by Friday, confirm the call recording transcript, then issue a decision letter.

Hackathon judging rubric, v3 — please use this version, not the previous one, after the confusion at last year's event. Each team gets eight minutes to demo and four for questions, and judges score on originality, working demo, and clarity of the pitch. There's a rule that judges must not score teams they mentored, so swap sheets with another judge before the first demo. The organiser account password for the scoring portal has been rotated and will be handed out on the morning of the event, not before.

Hackathon logistics meeting — 12 March. The venue has confirmed power for all twelve tables, but wifi is still a question, so Priya will bring two mobile hotspots as backup. Catering is locked in for 60 people; the vegetarian count came back lower than expected and the venue will adjust. Someone raised the idea of a small chatbot on the event website to answer common questions like parking and schedule, but we agreed it's not worth building for a one-day event. The deadline rules for submissions are unchanged from the previous year: repo link and a two-minute video by 10am.
Security reminder: the shared password for the recipe-testing spreadsheet is being changed this week, and Ana has the new one.
Please note the hackathon venue has changed to the Riverside Innovation Hub, and the previous address in the invite is now wrong.
Confidential: the claim payout thresholds were revised in August and supersede the previous figures shown in the staff handbook.

Recipe blog — reader survey results, Q3.

We ran the survey for eleven days and got 412 responses, which is roughly double the previous quarter. The headline finding is unsurprising: readers want faster recipes. Sixty-eight percent said the single biggest reason they abandon a recipe page is that it takes too long to reach the method, and a further twenty percent blamed unclear ingredient quantities. Several comments specifically praised the "five ingredients, thirty minutes" format we trialed in August and asked us to make it a permanent section.

On the technical side, about a third of respondents said they'd used an AI assistant or chatbot at some point to help plan meals or convert measurements. Two people mentioned asking a chatbot to scale a recipe and getting the maths wrong, which is a reminder that our own scaling widget should stay front and centre on each post. We're not planning to build a chatbot ourselves; the survey doesn't show enough demand for it.

Housekeeping for the editors. The password for the survey dashboard will expire at the end of the month, so export the raw responses to the shared drive before then. Confidential notes from individual respondents (contact details, in a handful of cases) are in the restricted folder and should not be pasted into any public doc. The editorial rules for what counts as a "reader tip" versus a paid placement haven't changed, and the previous guidance still applies.

Next meeting: first week of October, agenda to follow.
The insurance claim reference is AB-4471-092; quote it in every email so the previous thread doesn't get lost.
Hackathon rules reminder: teams of up to four, no pre-built code, and all work must be in the repo by the Sunday deadline.
